text:
Alex K: Heads up — Borealis is looking to run a 2-week POC starting next Monday. Main asks: onboard a new custom model variant (borealis-3b-compact), clarify KV cache behavior for long-context prompts, customer-managed KMS + EU data residency, and a pricing ballpark. Can we assemble a short runbook and checklist? Anyone available for a quick sync?

Mira S: tagging Sam P for infra/KV, Priya R for security, Kevin L for pricing. Also cc LegalOps for residency/SOW.

Sam P: I can own KV and routing. Quick question — does their encoder produce many long prefixes? If typical requests hit >8k tokens we should route to a long-context variant or enable chunked KV caching. Note: quantized variants may change tokenization edge behavior.

Alex K: Confirmed — their integration uses multi-doc prompts, often ~12k tokens. They also care about streaming responses and having a canary fallback.

Sam P: Proposal for routing policy: if request.tokens > 8000 -> route to borealis-3b-long, else -> borealis-3b-compact. Add fallback policy: on OOM or slow tails, failover to llama-13b-quant with degraded perf but guaranteed availability. I'll add this to the runbook.

Priya R: For the security questionnaire we need: data flow diagram, whether any customer data leaves their VPC, KMS key access policy (customer-managed vs our managed), retention windows, and if HSM is required. Also ask whether SOC2/HIPAA compliance is required.

Alex K: Borealis has requested SOC2 and EU data residency. They prefer customer-managed KMS if possible.

Kevin L: For POC pricing I suggest: sandbox (free), reserved capacity rate during POC ($X/hr) + usage cap. Need expected QPS and avg tokens/sec to finalize. Sam — can you estimate GPU hours for 1k sessions/day (avg 200 tokens/session vs 1k tokens/session scenarios)?

Sam P: Quick back-of-envelope: with batching + prefix caching, ~8 GPU-hours/day on A100 for 1k sessions @200 tokens/session. If average session is ~1k tokens (and more KV churn) expect ~20–24 GPU-hours/day. I'll put a short table in the sheet with low/med/high estimates.

Alex K: Shared runbook sheet (placeholder): https://go.redwood/sales/borealis-poc-runbook — please add your sections. Running checklist: onboarding steps, infra pre-reqs (VPC peering, KMS setup), security docs, pricing approvals, kickoff date, canary plan + rollback.

Priya R: I'll draft standard answers for KMS/data flow and customer-managed key redlines. Also will mark EU data residency clauses for LegalOps.

LegalBot: Looping in LegalOps — this will need an SOW addendum for data residency + indemnities.

LegalOps: Acknowledged. We'll draft an addendum and aim for a 1-business-day turnaround on initial draft. Need precise retention and transfer details from Priya.

Mira S: Ops question — do we recommend dedicated capacity for the POC? My vote: dedicated (predictable latency) if they can commit to a small reservation; otherwise use shared with burst and strict rate limits. Also preconfigure canary route and traffic split.

Alex K: Owners: Sam -> infra & runbook, Priya -> security questionnaire, Kevin -> pricing, LegalOps -> SOW. Please update the sheet by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:

Sam P: Will do — pushed initial runbook section (routing policy, fallback, estimated GPU hours).

Kevin L: I'll draft the POC pricing email and add tiered options.

Priya R: Preparing security Qs and a template response.

Mira S: I'll schedule a 30m sync for Monday to walk through the runbook. Invite sent.

Alex K: Thanks all — let's aim to have the doc and SOW draft ready before the kickoff.
